help.intro: An article is a shell plus one content entry per language. Status controls whether it is live; visibility controls who may read it once it is.
help.step_1_title: Write the content, one language at a time
help.step_1_body: Each language needs its own title, slug and body - the language tabs are separate entries, not translations of one record. A slug must be unique, and it is what the public URL uses.
help.step_2_title: File it under categories and tags
help.step_2_body: Categories place the article in the site tree; tags drive the "similar articles" box, which matches on every tag the article carries.
help.step_3_body: Public is readable by anyone. Restricted hands the article to a rule - a password, for instance - and a visitor without it gets a 404 rather than a prompt, so the article's existence stays hidden.
help.step_4_body: Articles start as draft and go draft → pending → published (or rejected, back to draft). Scheduled is what a future Publish At produces; a daily job flips it to published on the day.
help.step_5_title: Feature it, if it belongs in a slot
help.step_5_body: Featured status puts the article in the section or category slot; Order arranges the whole group at once. Featured Until drops it out of that group on the day given, without unpublishing it.
help.note: Only published articles reach the public API, and a restricted one stays out of every listing. The dashboard list is the only place that can address an article whatever its status.
